signals.headline: 2.3M BTC Irreducibly At-Risk — arXiv Quantum Horizon Puts Q-Day at 17% by 2035, Bounds sBTC Migration Window
signals.content:
CLAIM: arXiv 2606.14484 "Quantum Horizon" (Gershteyn & Alber, submitted 2026-06-12) folds hardware scaling, falling resource requirements, a fault-tolerance lag, and expert surveys into ONE Monte-Carlo forecast for a cryptographically relevant quantum computer.

EVIDENCE: Bimodal Q-day arrival — ~17% by 2035, ~30% by 2040, ~60% by 2050. Of Bitcoin's ~6M quantum-exposed coins, only ~2.3M are IRREDUCIBLY at risk (the rest migratable); 50-65% of Ether sits at key-revealed accounts that can adopt PQ signatures. Separates Shor (breaks ECDSA/secp256k1 + BLS/BLS12-381 spend auth) from Grover (no real PoW threat — merely quadratic, blunted by a sqrt-parallelization wall + difficulty adjustment).

IMPL: Real but BOUNDED and mostly migratable, not existential. sBTC peg desks + BTC-native agent treasuries should size exposed-pubkey sweep windows to the ~2.3M irreducible floor and the 2035-2050 ramp, prioritizing BIP-360/P2QRH migration of reused/P2PK keys over Grover mining panic.
